(p-٤٠٦)Surat al-Falaq: its purpose

Seeking refuge from the evil of everything that the created order, both outward and inward, has split open from. Its name, which clearly indicates this, is: "In the name of Allah," to whom belongs all power and strength; "the Most Merciful," who has gathered perfect bounty; "the Most Compassionate," who has bestowed complete gifts upon the people of His love, granting them safety from harmful speech.

When Allah, glorified and exalted, opened this Wise Remembrance with guidance in His saying ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatiha: 6], and with guidance and piety, which is the emblem of the penitent, in His saying ﴿A guidance for those who are mindful of Allah﴾ [al-Baqara: 2], and that is the first of the stations of those who seek shelter, He concluded it with affirming the matter of monotheism (tawhid) in a manner that cannot be conceived as more perfect than it, and with affirming sincerity (ikhlas) in it, as the command with "Say" (qul) indicates. That is the final station (nihaya al-maqamat) according to the knowers of God (al-arifin). Thus the religion was completed and the journey of the wayfarers came to its end. The closing of Surat al-Ikhlas affirms this by stating that He, exalted, has no equal, so the motives to devote oneself to Him and to cling to Him became abundant.

؎And it cast its staff and settled therein the home, / just as the eye is comforted by the returning traveler.

* *

He commanded seeking refuge with the Lord of this religion, in harmony with ﴿You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help﴾, from (p-٤٠٧) the evil of whatever harms it, outwardly or inwardly, and these are the creatures, even to the point of perishing in what is thought to be wealth. He began with what encompasses the devils of mankind and jinn, outwardly and inwardly, then followed with what encompasses both kinds and specifically the inward, whose soundness entails the soundness of the outward, informing of the nobility of the inward in a manner that does not harm the outward. In this there is an indication of encouragement to repeat the recitation from the beginning of the Qur'an, as His saying indicates: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an﴾ [al-Nahl: 98], meaning, when you intend to recite it, ﴿seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾ [al-Nahl: 98]. Then He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning, to everyone who receives the word from among all creatures, as instruction and command, for they are all nurtured and subdued, having no deliverance from any harm except by His protection, glorified and exalted. So each of them should, at the first affliction that befalls him, turn to his Master, who is able to remove it, to make his reliance (tawakkul) sound, for he thereby ascends to the state of contentment with the bitter decree. He should not take to relying on his own steadfastness and planning, by his own power and strength, for then his regret intensifies and that does not avert anything from him at all. ﴿I seek refuge﴾ [meaning] I seek protection, take shelter, hold fast, and guard myself.

Since this meaning is most fitting to the attribute of Lordship, because seeking refuge from harms is the greatest form of nurturing, He said: ﴿with the Lord of the daybreak﴾, meaning the One who nurtures it and brings forth from it whatever He wills. It is the thing split open by His bringing into being out of the darkness of non-existence, like the springs that split open the darkness of the earth and the mountains, and like the rains that split open the darkness of the atmosphere and the clouds, and like the plants that split open the darkness of the soil, and like the children that split open the darkness of the wombs, and like the dawn that splits the darkness of the night, and whatever moves from loneliness to what results from all of that of tranquility, calm, intimacy, and joy, and to other things among all the rest of the created beings. Al-Malawi said: "Falaq, with a sukun or a fatha, is everything from which the darkness of non-existence has split and by which all existing things have been brought into being." End of quote. It is specifically used in common usage for the dawn, so it is said: "falaq al-subh" (the splitting of dawn). From it is His saying: ﴿Splitter of the dawn﴾ [al-An'am: 96], because it clearly shows a change of state and imitates the Day of Resurrection, which is the greatest splitting, cleaving the darkness of annihilation and destruction through resurrection and revival. For the One who is able to do what precedes it, by what we witness, is able to do it, since there is no difference. Rather, resurrection is easier according to the customs of people, since it is a restoration, and likewise all other possible things. Whoever is able to do that is able to protect the one who seeks refuge from everything he fears and dreads.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 113, verse 2:

When things were of two kinds, the world of creation (ʿĀlam al-Khalq) and the world of command (ʿĀlam al-Amr), and the world of command was entirely good, evil was confined to the world of creation alone, and so for seeking refuge (bi-l-istiʿādhah) He, may He be exalted, said in generalising terms: ﴿From the evil of what He has created﴾, that is, from everything other than Allah, may He be exalted and mighty, and His attributes. Evil is sometimes voluntary, coming from the rational being who falls under the scope of "no" (lā) and from other living creatures, such as disbelief, injustice, the biting of beasts of prey (1)(p-409) and the stinging of venomous creatures; and sometimes natural, such as the burning of fire and the destruction caused by poisons.

The Imam Abu Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr said: "It has already been indicated (that is, in the discussion of the connection of Surah al-Ikhlas) to the aspect of its connection a moment ago, and that is clear, if Allah the Most High wills." End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 113, verse 3:

Since the conjunction of the specific to the general (*'atf al-khass 'ala al-'amm*, the mention of a particular item after a general category) indicates that the specific item is the most fitting of the general category's members for the ruling mentioned about it, and since darkness is the worst of things, for it is the root of all corruption, and since its evil, along with the evil of sorcery and envy, is hidden, He singled it out from among what creation shares in, because the hidden comes from where a person does not expect, and so it is more harmful. For this reason it was said: "The worst of enemies is the one who conceals hostility." The root *gh-s-q* revolves around darkness and pouring forth. *Al-ghasaq* (with a vowel pattern of *fa'al*) is the darkness of the early part of the night. *Ghasaqat al-'ayn* means the eye became dark or wept. *Al-laban* means milk poured from the udder. *Al-layl* means its darkness intensified. *Al-ghasaqan* (with the same vowel pattern) means pouring forth. *Al-ghasiq* is the moon, and it seems it was named so because of the swiftness of its movement and its pouring through the mansions (*al-burudj*), and because it has nothing of its own except darkness. *Al-Thurayya*, when it sets, and Allah knows best. Al-Fayruzabadi said in *al-Qamus* that this is because of the abundance of plagues and diseases when it sets. *Al-dhikr*, when it stands erect, as a group of scholars said and as was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and it is a cause of ignorance, which is entirely darkness. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And from the evil of the darkening one﴾, that is, of the one that is dark, cold, and pouring forth, whose darkness and coldness pour down, whether it is the root of darkness, sensory or immaterial, or whether it is a motivator toward it, like the male organ when it stands erect, because of the evil whisperings it leads to through the dominance of desire and the firm establishment of the rule of passion, and like the moon, because of the corrupting moisture that arises from it, which harms bodies, and other things, pouring forth with the utmost force, like the pouring of what overflows from fullness as it descends. He made it indefinite to indicate that not every darkening one is blameworthy, and Allah knows best.

Since the thing characterized by darkness thickens, its pouring and descent intensify until it settles and becomes firmly fixed in what it has been directed toward, gathered very tightly, like the gathering of a thing in a *waqba*, which is a hollow in a rock, and since the harm of darkness does not intensify except when it settles and remains, He spoke, using the particle of certainty: ﴿when it becomes intense﴾, that is, its darkness thickens and enters things with the utmost force, like something heavy and dense that is poured into a hollow that is like a well in a hard, smooth rock. This indicates that its treatment and removal are easy before it becomes firmly established. In the hadith: "When he saw that the sun had set (*waqabat*), he said: 'This is the time of its permissibility (*hall*),'" meaning the Maghrib prayer. And in Abu Ya'la's narration: "He said to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning the moon: 'Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this darkening one when it becomes intense.'" Most of the opinions hold that it is the night, and it was singled out for seeking refuge because harms are abundant in it and difficult to repel. The root of *ghasaq* is darkness, which entails fullness. It was also said that fullness is the root. The root of *wuqub* is entering a *waqba* or what is like a *waqba*, which is a hollow.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on Surah 113, verse 4:

Since sorcery is the greatest manifestation of the darkness of evil, firmly rooted in the veins and penetrating to their core, because of what it entails of separating a man from his wife, his father, his son, and the like, and what it entails of wasting away of bodies and killing of souls, he followed this with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And from the evil﴾.

Since every sorcerer is an evildoer, unlike the one who brings darkness (al-ghasiq) and the envier (al-hasid), and since sorcery is more harmful than the darkness and envy, in that it is entirely evil and in that it is more hidden than other things, and since what comes from women of it is greater, because the basis of its soundness and the strength of its effect is little intellect and religion, bad disposition, weakness of certainty, and quickness to be swayed, and women are more deeply rooted in each of these qualities and more firmly established in them, and since what proceeds from it in plural form and in the manner of intensification is greater than other forms, He used the masculine and the intensive form and the feminine so that what is less than it would be included by way of priority. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿the blowers﴾ [i.e., the souls] that practice sorcery, whether they are the souls of men or the souls of women, i.e., (p. 412) those who exaggerate in *nafth*, which is *tafl* (spitting), and is blowing together with some saliva. This is how it is in *al-Kashshaf*. The author of *al-Qamus* said: it is like blowing and less than *tufl*, and he said: *tafala* means he spat. In *al-Tafsir*, from al-Zajjaj, it is that it is *tufl* without saliva.

﴿in the knots﴾ [i.e.,] which they tie for sorcery in threads and the like. The occasion of revelation of this was that a Jew bewitched the Prophet (ﷺ), and he fell ill, as its transmission will come. Sorcery affects illness by the permission of Allah, exalted is He, and may reach the point of killing. So if the sorcerer confesses that he killed by his sorcery, and it is of that which usually kills, he is put to death for it according to al-Shafi'i. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 67) does not contradict this, as its explanation has passed in al-Ma'idah. Nor does this necessitate the truthfulness of the disbelievers in describing him (ﷺ) as one who has been bewitched, for they only intended madness or what resembles it of corruption and disorder of the intellect, and the exaggeration that whatever he says has no reality, just as what arises from one who has been bewitched is mixed up, and its reality cannot be known.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 113, verse 5 (part 1 of 2):**

Since the greatest motive for sorcery and for other harm done to people is envy (*hasad*), which is the wish for the removal of the blessing enjoyed by the envied person:

*I have been tolerant with all people except the envier, whose tolerance is rare and whose favour is hard to obtain.*

*How can a man be tolerant toward one who envies a blessing, when nothing satisfies him except its removal?*

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And from the evil of an envier﴾, meaning one who is firmly characterised by envy and deeply rooted in it [p. 413]. He used the indefinite form because not every envier is blameworthy. The greatest of envious ones is Satan, whose only constant occupation is striving to remove the blessings of worship from the human being through heedlessness.

Since the harm of envy lies only in what is manifested and acted upon by its demands, through striking with the evil eye or otherwise, He qualified it, saying: ﴿when he envies﴾, meaning when he envies in actual deed with his envious eye. As for when envy is not manifested, it harms no one but the envier himself, due to his distress at another's blessing. The implication of the verse is a supplication for the blessings of both abodes that one might be envied for, because the best of people is one who lives envied and dies envied. Whoever does not pay attention to supplicating for this and does not strive to obtain what would make him envied, Iblis laughs at him when he recites this verse, because he has no virtue for which he could be envied. Perhaps He expressed it with the particle of confirmation (*inna*-type emphasis, *idhā*) to indicate that whoever is firmly established in envy and capable of being characterised by it, what the expression of the attribute implies is that its manifestation from him is certain, and that in most cases no one can resist it except those whom Allah the Exalted protects.

He who knows that envy is the cause of sorcery, which leads to killing, the greatest of sins after polytheism and including polytheism (since sorcery cannot be valid in any true sense except with polytheism), knows that envy is the worst thing from which the darkness of non-existence splits open. The evidence for this is its dominance over earlier nations and the warning to this Community, which is "the best community brought forth for mankind" [Qur'an 3:110] [p. 414], against it, on the testimony of its guide (ﷺ). Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"The disease of the nations before you has crept upon you: envy and hatred. Verily, hatred is the shaver; I do not say it shaves hair, but it shaves away the religion."

Similar reports are narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with them). The greatest causes of this shaving, or all of them, are envy. Thus it is known that the end of the surah returns to its beginning, and its joint bends back upon its connection. Whoever is protected from these mentioned things, his heaven of heart splits open (?) to the sun of knowledge after the darkness of the night of ignorance, and its horizons shine with the lights of wisdom, until description becomes too narrow to contain the wonders of unveiling:

*There you see what fills the eye with delight, and what consoles every stranger for his homeland.*

Thus attachment to anything other than Allah is severed, through pure following and distance from innovation, in accordance with the words: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me, and Allah will love you﴾ [Qur'an 3:31]. The command to seek refuge has invalidated the claim of the Jabriyya (Determinists), who say: "We are like a tool with no action of our own at all; we are like a stone that moves only when moved." For if He were the one moving us without our choice, the command would have no purpose. It has also invalidated the claim of the Qadariyya (Free-Willers), who say: "We create our own actions," and the claim of the philosophers, who say that when the cause and the effect exist, the influence occurs without need for a divine connection, like fire and firewood. For if that were so, these effects, the causes and their effects, would have occurred from their agents who are the causes, or the actions which are the causes, and the effects which are the bodies whose influence is intended, would have been affected, and seeking refuge would have been of no benefit. But the evidence contradicts this. The doctrine of the Ash'ariyya, the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), is established: when the cause and the effect exist, the existence of the result depends on Allah the Exalted's bringing it into being. If He makes the cause take effect, the result exists; if He does not, it does not exist.

The two surahs inform us that afflictions are numerous and that He is capable of repelling them. Thus they bring one to fear and hope, and that is the essence of servanthood. The occasion of the revelation of the two protectors (al-mu'awwidhatayn), according to what al-Wahidi reported from the exegetes, may Allah's mercy be upon them all, and al-Baghawi from Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with them), is that: "A boy from the Jews used to serve the Prophet (ﷺ). The Jews approached him and kept at him until he took a comb from the head of the Prophet (ﷺ) and several of its teeth. He gave them to the Jews, who used them to work sorcery upon him. This was carried out by Labid ibn al-A'sam, a Jew. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, his hair became disordered, and he would imagine that he was having intercourse with his wives while not actually doing so. He was wasting away without knowing what afflicted him. Then one day, while he was sleeping, two angels came to him. One sat at his head and the other at his feet. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: 'What is wrong with the man?' He said: 'He has been bewitched.' He said: 'And who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn al-A'sam, the Jew.' He said: 'And with what did he bewitch him?' He said: 'With a comb and combings.' He said: 'And where is it?' He said: 'In the sheath of a male date-palm spathe, under a rock (*rā'ūfa*), in the well of Dhi Arwan, a well belonging to the Banu Zuraiq.' The *juff* is the husk of the spathe, and the *rā'ūfa* is a stone at the bottom of the well upon which the one drawing water stands." The Prophet (ﷺ) awoke and said to 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her): "O 'A'isha! Did you not realise that Allah informed me of my ailment!" Then he sent 'Ali, al-Zubayr and 'Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with them), and they drained the well until it looked like the soaking water of henna. Then they removed the rock and took out the *juff*. Inside it were the combings from his head and the teeth of his comb, and a taut cord in which there were eleven knots, stuck with needles. Then Allah the Exalted sent down the two surahs, the two protectors, which together contain eleven verses: al-Falaq has five and al-Nas has six. Whenever he recited a verse, a knot was untied, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) felt relief until the last knot was untied, and he got up as if released from a bond. Jibril (peace be upon him) kept saying: ''In the name of Allah, I perform ruqyah for you from everything that harms you, from an envier, from an evil eye, and Allah will heal you.''" They said: "O Messenger of Allah! Shall we not take him out and kill him?" He said: "As for me, Allah has healed me, and I dislike that I should stir up evil among the people." In another narration: "He (ﷺ) went to the well himself, then returned to 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) and said: 'By Allah, its water is as if it were the soaking water of henna, and its palm trees are as if they were the heads of devils.' I said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah! Why did you not bring him out?' He said: 'As for me, Allah has healed me, and I disliked stirring up evil among the people.'" It may be reconciled that he went to it in his noble person and did not bring it out, then he felt some pain and sent for it, and it was brought out, and all the pain disappeared. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was bewitched until he imagined he had done a thing when he had not done it. Then one day, while he was with me, he supplicated Allah and supplicated, then said: 'Do you realise, O 'A'isha, that Allah the Exalted has given me a ruling on what I asked Him about?' I said: 'And what is that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Two angels came to me...'" and he mentioned it. Al-Nasa'i in his Sunan in the chapter on warfare (*al-muharaba*), Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, Ahmad ibn Mani', 'Abd ibn Humayd, and Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili in their Musnads, and al-Baghawi in his Tafsir, all narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "A man used to enter upon the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) [p. 418] and he would take for him... A man from the Jews bewitched the Prophet (ﷺ), and he complained of it for some days. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said:

[p-419] "A man from the Jews bewitched you. He tied knots for you in a well of such-and-such, or he said: he threw them into the well of a man of the Ansar. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent people, and they extracted it and brought it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) untied it. Every time he untied a knot, he found some lightness, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up as if he had been released from a fetter. He never mentioned that to that Jew, nor was it ever seen in his face." And in another narration: "Two angels came to him and sat, one at his head and the other at his feet. One of them said: 'Do you know what his ailment is?' The other said: 'The one who has bewitched him has tied knots for him and thrown them into a well.' So he sent a man to him, and in another narration, Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and he took the knots and found that the water had turned yellow. He said: He took the knots and untied them, and he was healed. After that, the man would come in to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he did not mention anything to him, nor did he reproach him about it."

This grace is a benefit of the two Mu'awwidhatan (the two surahs of seeking refuge), just as Allah granted it to His Messenger (ﷺ), so He has likewise bestowed it upon the rest of his community. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi related it, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic). [And] al-Nasa'i related it with a musnad or mursal chain. Al-Nawawi said: "With sound chains" (p-419 continues), from Abdullah ibn Khubayb (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Recite Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad and the two Mu'awwidhatan when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, [three times], and they will suffice you against everything." The narrations concerning the virtue of these three surahs are very numerous.

He made the seeking of refuge in two surahs an indication of the recommendation of repeating it, and made them eleven verses together, as an exhortation to increase it by repetition. The Falaq, which has five verses, was placed first, together with what preceded regarding the correspondences (munasabat, the connections between surahs and verses), because its pairing with the surah of Tawhid is more fitting. He made it a pair (shaf') with the surah of al-Nas, which has six verses, which is more fitting, so that the pair is with a pair, and the beginning is with an odd number after the surah of Witr (the odd). The essential meaning of this great surah, in its most wondrous and sublime sense, is seeking refuge in Allah by mentioning His name al-Rabb (the Lord), which requires beneficence and nurture, by bringing blessings and warding off calamities, from the evil of what He created, and from sorcery and envy. Just as most of al-Baqarah corresponds to it in returning the end to the beginning, since it is the second of the first, so this is the second of the last, in mentioning the enemies of the Prophet (ﷺ) who envied him for what he was given of blessings, and in reminding them of the blessings Allah granted them which they rejected. Most of that concerns the Children of Israel, who were the most envious of people toward him (ﷺ). Among the greatest things by which they went astray was sorcery, referred to by the words of the Exalted: (p-420) ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾ [al-Baqarah: 102], until He said: ﴿And they learned from the two what they could use to separate a man from his wife﴾ [al-Baqarah: 102], until He said: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your belief, out of envy from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109]. Sorcery was among the greatest effects of their plotting upon the Prophet (ﷺ), until the two Mu'awwidhatan were revealed concerning it, and the sorcerer was one of them.

With this, what Allah has facilitated of speech concerning the coherence of its meanings according to the structure of its words has been concluded. What remains is speech about its words in terms of number, regarding what it indicates of blessings and reinforcements. [The surah] has twenty-three words, an indication that in the twenty-third year of prophethood he (ﷺ) would be safe from the harm of his envious ones; this is by death at the completion of the religion and the despair of the envious from any harm in religion and worldly life, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) deliverance from every turbidity. If you add to them the pronouns, which are five, they become twenty-eight, which corresponds to the year fifteen after the Hijrah, and that is when the affair of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) became firmly established in the second year of his caliphate, by dispatching armies and sending them to the kings of Persia and Rome, and his awe penetrated their hearts; the Persians were humbled by the victory of the Arabs over Rustam, their greatest commander, and the Romans by their victory over Mahan, their greatest chief. Thus the affair of the hypocrites and the envious was annihilated, and they despaired of the influence of even the smallest plot by any of the plotters. If the four words of the Basmalah are added to them, they become thirty-two. If you count from the beginning of prophethood, this corresponds to the nineteenth year after the Hijrah, and in it was the conquest of Caesarea [of Rome], in the lands of al-Sham (Syria). With its conquest was the conquest of all the lands of al-Sham; no town remained there except that it was in the hands of the Muslims, and the state of Rome departed from it. In it also was the conquest of Jalula', in the lands of Persia, which was a very great conquest that broke their armies and their kings, and for this it was named the Conquest of Conquests. At that time came the greatest disgrace upon the Persians and the Romans, who were the most envious of the envious, given the might and strength they had through wealth and men. And if you count from the Hijrah, it corresponds to the year of the extinction of the kingdom of the greatest of the envious, the Khosrows, whose kingdom was torn apart by the letter of the Prophet (ﷺ), who sent to his governor Badhan, whom he had appointed over the lands of Yemen, ordering him to attack the Prophet (ﷺ). So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that He, glorified is He, would kill him on a night He named. When that night came, the Prophet (ﷺ) informed the messengers of Badhan of this, and they returned to Badhan and informed him. He said: "If he is truthful, then the news will come on such-and-such a day." The news came on that day, confirming his truthfulness (ﷺ). (p-422) Badhan and those with him of the Persians who were in the lands of Yemen embraced Islam, and none of them stayed behind. He sent a delegation of them to the Prophet (ﷺ) with this news. Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) took charge of them, may Allah be pleased with them all. And Allah knows best.
